sections.heading: What Our Oil Leak & Gasket Repair Service Involves

blocks.html: Oil leaks are common on older Mercedes-Benz engines, particularly from gaskets that harden and shrink over time. We repair leaks at the source, using OEM-quality parts and Mercedes-approved sealants to ensure a permanent fix.
Depending on the location of the leak, our process includes:

items: **Valve cover gasket replacement** - the most common leak point. We remove intake components, clean sealing surfaces thoroughly, install new gaskets with correct sealant at joints, and torque to factory specifications. On V6/V8 engines, both banks are done together to save time and prevent future leaks.

**Timing cover gasket repair** - a more involved job. We drain oil, remove auxiliaries and the harmonic balancer, replace the cover gasket and front crankshaft seal, and reinstall with fresh sealant. This also gives us the opportunity to inspect timing components.
**Oil pan / sump gasket** - we drain oil, remove the sump, clean old gasket material, and install new gasket or sealant (some models use only sealant).
**Oil filter housing gasket** - we remove the housing, clean both mating faces to bare metal, and install a new OEM-spec gasket, torqued to specification.
**Additional seals** - we also check and replace spark plug tube seals, oil filler cap O-rings, and camshaft adjuster seals where needed.

blocks.html: Every repair is followed by a thorough test to confirm no residual leakage. All work carries our **12-month unlimited-mileage warranty** on parts and labour.
The cost of oil leak repair depends on the location and extent of the leak. We provide a fixed-price quote after inspection - no hidden extras.

steps.title: Inspection & Diagnosis
steps.body: We visually inspect the engine for oil traces, using UV dye if needed to pinpoint the exact source. We determine which gasket or seal is leaking.

steps.title: Preparation
steps.body: We drain oil, remove necessary components to access the leaking gasket - this may include intake parts, auxiliaries, or the harmonic balancer.

steps.title: Cleaning
steps.body: We meticulously clean all mating surfaces to bare metal - the quality of cleaning is the single most important factor for long-term repair success.

steps.title: Gasket & Seal Replacement
steps.body: We install new OEM-quality gaskets or apply Mercedes-approved sealant (Drei Bond 1209) to the correct areas, following factory torque sequences.

steps.title: Reassembly & Refill
steps.body: We refit all removed components, refill with fresh oil, and replace any lost coolant (if timing cover was removed).

steps.title: Testing & Handover
steps.body: We run the engine to operating temperature, check for any new leaks, and perform a road test. Your vehicle is returned with a 12-month warranty.

items.q: What are the most common oil leak points on a Mercedes-Benz?
items.a: Valve cover gaskets, oil filter housing gaskets, timing cover seals, and oil pan gaskets are the most frequent sources. We repair all of them.

items.q: How long does an oil leak repair take?
items.a: Valve cover gaskets typically take a day. Timing cover repairs are more involved and may take 1-2 days. We always give you a time estimate before starting.

items.q: Do you use genuine Mercedes parts?
items.a: We use OEM-quality gaskets and Mercedes-approved sealants (Drei Bond 1209) - never generic alternatives that can fail prematurely.

items.q: Do you provide a warranty on gasket repairs?
items.a: Yes. All our oil leak repairs come with a 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty covering parts and labour.
Yes - we offer nationwide recovery from £70 (separate charge). We can arrange collection and delivery back to you.

items.q: Why is cleaning so important for gasket repairs?
items.a: Proper cleaning of mating surfaces is the single most important factor for long-term success. Any residual oil or old gasket material will prevent a proper seal and cause the leak to return.
